meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. Was Owen heard before that zero went in?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What is the zero based on?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in from somewhere else. Did you ask him that before you entered anything?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays out of his classroom. Who else has seen that screen?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong act and scene is a citation error, Hale. You take marks off for that, you don't zero the essay. And you didn't answer me: who else has seen this?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Twice now you've passed over who else has seen this, and that goes in my email. What are you asking for?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
He changed his mind in two weeks. That's what an outline is for. Now answer me: what do you want from him?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I'll hold you to tonight. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Give me a date, and the mark goes in well before December 1.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. He'll be here. Put the time and the room in tonight's email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School
Subject: Owen Kalinowski, English 30-1

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want to know who else has seen what you showed me and whether Owen was asked anything before the zero was entered, along with the time and room for Thursday and the new mark entered before December 1. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants it confirmed in writing tonight with a time and room, and answers on who else has seen your evidence and whether Owen was heard first. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it with time to spare.

What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then met her pasted-it-in defence by offering to look at any dated draft Owen brings. It was dated, tied to his own work and something she could check herself.

What cost ground: You twice passed over her question about who else had seen your evidence. She watches procedure more closely than anything, and that gap is now in an email copied to the principal.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop. Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's creation at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, the night before it was due, which is a late October night very close to the one she is avoiding. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asked who else had seen that screen, answer in one plain sentence before you turn to the Hamlet quotation, so no procedural question is left open for her email.
